records.summary: The idea is a CSV normalizer that imports foreign-currency bank transactions into UK bookkeeping software. It would add exchange-rate and MTD record support to an export-and-import workflow.
records.customer: Self-employed people using UK bookkeeping software with foreign-currency accounts.

competitors.name: FreeAgent
competitors.price: £19/month; £0 for eligible NatWest, RBS, Ulster Bank or Mettle customers
competitors.note: Official Wise feed, multi-currency accounts, MTD Income Tax and CSV statement uploads.

competitors.name: Xero
competitors.price: £55/month for Comprehensive; £70/month for Ultimate after the introductory period
competitors.note: Official Wise sync, multi-currency feeds and MTD Income Tax.

competitors.name: TaxMTD
competitors.price: Free to £129/month; Business plan lists multi-currency at £39/month annual or £49 monthly
competitors.note: Advertises Wise and Revolut multi-currency feeds; launch and plan details unverified.

competitors.name: Pippa
competitors.note: Plans cross-currency FX at HMRC spot rate for later in 2026; not launched.

competitors.name: Clear Books
competitors.price: MTD plans £0/£5/£15; Large plan £44/month plus VAT
competitors.note: MTD plans exclude multi-currency feeds; multi-currency listed on Large.

competitors.name: QuickFile
competitors.price: Power User £60/year plus VAT; bank feeds £15/year plus VAT
competitors.note: Supports foreign-currency bank accounts and custom CSV statement imports.

competitors.name: ofxstatement-wise
competitors.note: Open-source tool that converts Wise CSV exports to OFX.

rounds.plain: The check found fewer than two dated recent launches for this specific need. It noted that Clear Books' MTD Income Tax plan excludes foreign-currency feeds.

K3 means a platform owner or partner already serves the need. Wise integrates with FreeAgent and Xero, and FreeAgent can be free for eligible customers; the sources say this leaves no lasting wedge for a separate formatter.

risks: Demand is not established: the September 2025 Reddit report could not be verified, and no other recent foreign-currency MTD-ITSA complaint was found.
The number of MTD users with foreign-currency accounts, search volume, and willingness to pay are unverified.
Wrong exchange rates could create liability and support work.
Owner time of 2–5 h/week is claimed but unverified.
records.moat: The sources find no lasting wedge: official Wise integrations and free or bundled alternatives cover the need. Free converters also handle the technical conversion core.

hours.note: Claimed; unverified. CSV format support and exchange-rate questions could add work.

records.next_steps: Recheck in about 6 months for complaints about FreeAgent or Xero handling Wise or Revolut FX badly, as the £30k cohort arrives in April 2027.

competitors.name: Paxton Advanced
competitors.note: The platform includes CSV transaction import, clipboard paste in supported fields, and an invoice/payment correction workflow.

risks: The reviewer’s paid-user status and subscription amount are unverified.
No direct third-party helper incumbents were found, but Paxton's existing features cover the described tasks.

records.summary: The idea is a keyboard-first data-entry layer or add-on for charity finance teams using accounting software with awkward form navigation. It would reduce extra mouse clicks where Tab does not move between some fields.
records.customer: Charity finance teams using accounting software such as Paxton.
records.market: England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland are discussed in the sources; the proposed customer geography is not specified.

competitors.name: Paxton Standard
competitors.note: Accounting product, not a direct keyboard-layer comparable; documents some keyboard operations.

competitors.name: Paxton Advanced
competitors.note: Accounting product, not a direct keyboard-layer comparable; documents some keyboard operations.

competitors.name: Data Developments MyFundAccounting
competitors.price: £15/month including VAT, plus £4 per additional licence
competitors.note: Accounting product, not a direct keyboard-layer comparable.

competitors.name: Andica Charity Accounts
competitors.note: Accounting product, not a direct keyboard-layer comparable.

competitors.name: Aedon.Charities
competitors.price: £145/month per full user and £40/month per reviewer
competitors.note: Accounting product, not a direct keyboard-layer comparable; includes 10 Salesforce cloud licences.

competitors.name: OneKey Navigator
competitors.note: Generic Firefox extension with 1 user shown; not an accounting form-navigation fix.

rounds.plain: Paxton documents some keyboard shortcuts and paste actions, but the sources do not establish that they fix the reported Tab-navigation gaps.
The sole specific complaint is self-reported, with no payment evidence. Cloud compatibility and whether the keyboard gap persists are unverified.

risks: The single specific complaint is self-reported; payment is unverified.
Whether Paxton's cloud client exposes a modifiable webpage DOM is unverified, and a browser extension would not cover its Windows desktop users.
Screen changes could break selectors; support workload and the <=5 hours/week limit are unverified.
The sources describe a discrepancy between Paxton's product page's monthly rolling contracts and online terms stating a one-calendar-year minimum.
records.moat: No strong moat is evidenced. A tested map of Paxton screens and a regression suite could help, but would be easy for Paxton to reproduce and would need maintenance.

hours.note: Unverified model constraint; screen changes and user support could add recurring work.

records.next_steps: Request Paxton's free trial and use dummy data to see whether the Tab gap still occurs. If it does, make a local-only Chrome content-script prototype for that form, record a before/after demo, and seek a paid pilot through an opt-in charity-finance channel; stop if the gap cannot be reproduced or no user commits.

records.summary: The idea is a searchable database of German public awards and competitors for contractors, trades, and manufacturers. Users would monitor awards and buyers, analyze bid activity, and export data.
records.how_money: Subscription pricing for monitoring, analysis and exports; Kontor Data lists €79/month plus VAT, cancellable monthly.

revenue_claims.claim: 199,334 public awards worth €135.2bn and 11,524 reporting offices for 2024

records.paid_demand: Kontor Data lists €79/month plus VAT, but no verified revenue or transaction evidence was found. The sources describe the price as an advertised price, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: Kontor Data
competitors.note: Offers the core company, buyer, award, bid-count and competitor analysis described in the idea.

competitors.name: TendiGo
competitors.note: Tender service; an advertised price, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: VergabeHero
competitors.note: Tender service; an advertised price, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: Patterno
competitors.note: Tender service; an advertised price, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: DTAD
competitors.note: Price unlisted in the sources.

competitors.name: ibau
competitors.note: Price unlisted in the sources.

competitors.name: Minerva
competitors.note: Sources describe buyer/supplier profiles and historical winner analysis.

competitors.name: aufträge.io
competitors.note: Sources describe historical winner analysis.

competitors.name: Tender Republic
competitors.note: Free searchable directory with award winners and values.

rounds.plain: The check described a normalized, sourced history of German awards, bidders and buyers as a possible data asset, while noting that source coverage, customer counts and payment evidence were unverified.
K0 means the moat is too weak to take 3+ months to copy. Existing analytics products and free official data make the proposed generic database reproducible.

risks: No verified revenue, customer payment, churn, or search-volume evidence was found.
The €79/month figure is an advertised price, not evidence of sales.
The proposed product overlaps with Kontor Data and other historical-award analytics; free official data is available.
Owner hours of <=5/week are unverified, and reliable nationwide coverage requires ongoing data work.
records.moat: A carefully deduplicated, source-linked history with reliable buyer and supplier matching could be a compiled-data asset, but the sources find that the proposed generic product is already served and reproducible. A stronger moat would require materially better coverage, identity resolution, or a unique dataset.

hours.note: Unverified; ongoing source monitoring and exception handling are implied, but workload is unknown.

records.next_steps: Choose one construction trade and region, create a small source-linked sample from official TED/DÖE records, and compare it with Tender Republic and Kontor results. Publish a labelled preview with an intended price and opt-in paid-pilot request; do not build the full database unless users identify a specific gap and accept the price.

records.summary: The idea is a self-serve contract feed and saved searches for suppliers pursuing Belgian and EU public work. The proposed data joins Belgian notices, TED records, and below-threshold opportunities.
records.how_money: Subscription plans; GPC Gov lists Essential from €758/year excl. VAT or €80/month and Professional from €1,299/year excl. VAT.
records.customer: Suppliers pursuing Belgian and EU public work.

revenue_claims.claim: Essential from €758/year excl. VAT or €80/month; Professional from €1,299/year excl. VAT
56,973 contracts registered on e-Procurement in 2024, of which 25,709 were published

records.paid_demand: GPC Gov lists subscription prices, but no verified revenue or payment event was found. Its claim of 500+ Belgian companies is unverified and conflicts with a client-company counter shown as 0.

competitors.name: GPC Gov
competitors.price: Essential from €758/year excl. VAT or €80/month; Professional from €1,299/year or €136/month
competitors.note: Advertises daily alerts and non-published below-threshold contracts; customer and coverage claims are unverified.

competitors.name: BOSA e-Procurement
competitors.note: Offers published opportunities and supplier search profiles with daily email alerts.

competitors.name: Polytender
competitors.note: Added Belgian BOSA coverage for published notices, including below-EU-threshold notices, on 22 Oct 2026; coverage of non-published contracts is unverified.

competitors.name: Aanbestedingsradar
competitors.price: free tier; Match €270/month billed annually; Bid Office €450/month billed annually
competitors.note: Live BOSA/TED matcher.

rounds.plain: The check treated a refreshed dataset of Belgian notices and below-threshold opportunities as a possible data asset, while noting that source coverage, customer counts and payment evidence were unverified.
K0 means the moat is too weak to take 3+ months to copy. The only potentially differentiated unpublished-opportunity feed lacks verified source provenance, payment evidence and willingness to pay.

risks: No verified revenue, payment event date, churn, customer count, or willingness-to-pay evidence.
The claim of 500+ companies conflicts with a homepage counter shown as 0.
The sources provide no public source-by-source evidence for the claimed non-published opportunities or their reuse rights.
Free BOSA search profiles and Polytender's Belgian BOSA coverage weaken the published-notice feed's differentiation.
records.moat: A data moat is only possible if the business can maintain a broader, fresher, source-linked dataset of actionable local opportunities that is lawfully reusable. The sources say the published-notice layer is substitutable; the claimed exclusive municipal-source coverage is unverified.

hours.note: Estimated target after steady state; depends on stable, permissioned sources and no bespoke curation or consulting.

records.next_steps: Manually inspect 20 GPC Gov records labelled unpublished. For each, record the original source URL, date, deadline/status, buyer and whether suppliers can access it without an invitation; compare with BOSA and Polytender, note duplicates and reuse terms, and verify access and rights before building collection.
